searchDocs.title: Spline​
searchDocs.content: </> type Spline = LinearSpline | CubicSpline | SampledSpline Any spline.

searchDocs.title: linear​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.linear( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → LinearSpline Straight segments between the points. Needs at least two points to make a segment.

searchDocs.title: bezier​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.bezier( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → CubicSpline Cubic Bezier curves: points 1-4 make the first curve, 4-7 the second, and so on, so it passes through every third point. Points past the last complete curve are kept but ignored.

searchDocs.title: hermite​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.hermite( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. velocities: {VectorLike}?,-- One per point. Missing ones are zero. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → CubicSpline Passes through every point, leaving each one with its velocity. Change velocities withCubicSpline:setVelocity.

searchDocs.title: cardinal​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.cardinal( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. scale: number,-- How strongly the curve follows its neighbours; 0.5 is Catmull-Rom. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → CubicSpline Passes through every point, with velocities of (next - previous) * scale. The end points mirror their only neighbour. Change the scale with CubicSpline:setScale.

searchDocs.title: catmullRom​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.catmullRom( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → CubicSpline A Splynx.cardinal spline with a scale of 0.5: passes through every point with natural-looking curves.

searchDocs.title: bSpline​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.bSpline( points: {VectorLike}?,-- Relative to the pivot. pivot: VectorLike?-- Defaults to the origin. ) → CubicSpline A uniform cubic B-spline: smooth everywhere, including across joints, but it only passes near its points. Needs at least four points.

searchDocs.title: sampled​
searchDocs.content: </> Splynx.sampled( source: LinearSpline | CubicSpline,-- The spline to copy. spacing: number-- Studs between samples, along the spline. ) → SampledSpline A static copy of source as straight segments spacing studs apart along it, for the fastest distance lookups. Smaller spacing follows curves more closely. It doesn't follow later edits to source; sample it again after changing it.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Spacing must be more than 0"	If `spacing` isn't positive. "Spline doesn't have enough points to make a curve"	If `source` has no curves.

searchDocs.title: getPos​
searchDocs.content: </> LinearSpline:getPos( alpha: number-- From 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). Clamped. ) → vector The position at alpha. Alpha splits evenly across segments, so with 4 segments, 0.25 is the end of the first. Since segments have different lengths, equal alpha steps don't move at a constant speed; use LinearSpline:getUniformPos or LinearSpline:getPosAtDistance for that.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Spline doesn't have enough points to make a segment"	If the spline has fewer than two points.

searchDocs.content: </> LinearSpline:sample(count: number) → {vector} count positions at evenly spaced alphas, including both ends. Faster than calling LinearSpline:getPos in a loop. Use LinearSpline:sampleUniform for positions evenly spaced along the length instead.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Spline doesn't have enough points to make a segment"	If the spline has fewer than two points.

searchDocs.content: </> LinearSpline:getLength() → number The length along the spline, or 0 if it has no segments.

searchDocs.content: </> LinearSpline:getAlphaAtDistance( distance: number,-- Studs from the start. Clamped to the length. hint: number?-- The hint returned by the previous lookup on this spline, if any. ) → ( number,-- The alpha, as used by LinearSpline:getPos. number-- A hint for the next lookup. ) The alpha at which distance along the spline has been travelled.

searchDocs.title: Errors
searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Spline doesn't have enough points to make a segment"	If the spline has fewer than two points.

searchDocs.title: getPosAtDistance​
searchDocs.content: </> LinearSpline:getPosAtDistance( distance: number,-- Studs from the start. Clamped to the length. hint: number?-- The hint returned by the previous lookup on this spline, if any. ) → ( vector, number-- A hint for the next lookup. ) The position distance studs along the spline. This is the call to use for things moving at a constant speed: keep a distance, add speed * deltaTime to it every frame, and pass back the hint from the last call. local distance, hint = 0, nil RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime) distance = (distance + speed * deltaTime) % spline:getLength() local position position, hint = spline:getPosAtDistance(distance, hint) end)

searchDocs.content: Type	Description"Spline doesn't have enough points to make a segment"	If the spline has fewer than two points.
